The 2022 Volvo XC60 B6 Inscription is a compact luxury SUV that leans heavily toward comfort, tech, and Scandinavian design rather than raw sportiness. It sits near the top of the XC60 lineup (below the plug-in hybrid models) and represents the most luxurious non-hybrid trim.

Heres a clean, real-world breakdown:

Overall vibe

Think of it as a refined, tech-forward luxury SUVnot flashy, but very upscale and calm. Volvo focuses on:

Clean, minimalist design
Safety tech
Comfortable ride over aggressive performance
Performance & engine
Engine: 2.0L turbo + supercharged inline-4 (mild hybrid system)
Power: ~295 hp/310 lb-ft
Drivetrain: Standard AWD
Transmission: 8-speed automatic
060 mph: ~5.9 seconds
MPG: ~24 combined

Its quick and smooth, but not meant to feel sporty like a BMWmore effortless and quiet.

What B6 means
B6 = mild hybrid performance engine
Uses a 48-volt system to:
Improve fuel efficiency
Smooth acceleration
Add a small power boost

Important: it cannot drive on electric power aloneit just assists the engine.

Interior (where it really shines)

The Inscription trim is all about luxury:

Nappa leather seats (ventilated + heated)
Real wood trim and metal accents
Crystal gear shifter (signature Volvo touch)
4-zone climate control
Extremely comfortable front seats

Volvo interiors are known for being clean, airy, and high-quality without feeling overdone.

Tech & infotainment
9-inch touchscreen with Google built-in system (Maps, Assistant, Play Store)
Apple CarPlay/Android Auto
12-inch digital gauge cluster
Harman Kardon premium sound
Wireless charging

The Google system is a standoutfeels more like a smartphone than traditional car software.

Size & practicality
Seats 5 passengers
Cargo space: ~29.7 cu ft (63+ max)
Towing: up to ~3,500 lbs

Its smaller than a Tahoemore in line with an X3 or Lexus RX.

Safety (Volvo strong point)
Blind spot monitoring
Lane keep assist
Automatic emergency braking
Pilot Assist (semi-autonomous highway driving)

Volvo is known for being one of the safest brands overall, and this model reflects that.

Price (when new)
Around $56K MSRP for B6 Inscription
What its best at
Comfort and daily driving
Interior quality and design
Safety tech
Quiet, smooth ride

A blistering 0-60 mph in just 2.5 seconds and handling precision that pushes the limits of what a road car can do. Behind the wheel, the cabin wraps the driver in Nero leather, with Ferrari's signature manettino steering wheel and carbon fiber reminding you of its performance intentions. It is a two-door, 2+2 hard top convertible which is powered by a 4.3L naturally aspirated V8 engine which can produce 453hp at 7,750rpm and 358lb/ft of torque at 5,000rpm. The California had a top speed of 193 mph and could accelerate from 060mph in 3.9 seconds.The car revives the name used on the late-1950s Ferrari 250 GT California Spyder and the 1960s 365 California. When introduced in 2008, the modern California represented Ferraris entrance into a 4th model category, (front-engine, eight cylinder, grand tourer). The California represented a radical new design by Pininfarina S.p.A. and was developed under the oversight of Ken Okuyama. The car's grand touring personality was emphasized with a slightly higher ride height compared to its more aggressive siblings. The chassis was designed and manufactured by Ferrari division Carrozzeria Scaglietti. Overall, it is considered a landmark car for Ferrari in that it represents a number of concepts being used for the first time in their road cars. These being: The first front engine Ferrari with a V8, the first to feature a 7-speed dual-clutch transmission, the first hard top convertible with a folding metal roof, the first with multi-link rear suspension and the first with direct petrol injection. Safety and Security
  • Forward collision mitigation - Forward thinking. You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. That's when the forward collision mitigation system comes to life. When it senses an impending impact, it will activate a combination of features to help prevent or reduce the severity of an accident. Forward collision mitigation is always looking ahead.
  • Pedestrian impact prevention - An extra step toward safety. Pedestrians don't always stop, look, and listen, but with Pedestrian Impact Prevention, your vehicle is equipped to better see them and avoid them. This system constantly monitors the road ahead to identify and track pedestrians. It projects that image to an interior display screen, AND should an impact become likely, Pedestrian impact prevention takes steps to avoid a collision.
  • Rear camera - Watching your back! The rear camera helps you see obstacles and hazards you otherwise couldn't by showing enhanced images of what is behind you. The rear camera is an extra set of eyes that's both convenient and safe.
Technology and Telematics

With The Gallery Guarantee, you’ll enjoy a 3-month/500-mile vehicle service contract and a multi-point safety inspection for ultimate peace of mind. Plus, explore exclusive warranty extension options and take advantage of our Buy Back Guarantee. It’s not just a purchase, it’s a promise that ensures your journey begins with confidence. This 2002 Pontiac Firebird Trans Am WS6 is far more than just a late-model muscle car—it’s a documented piece of Daytona 500 history with a story that sets it apart from virtually every other fourth-generation F-body on the market. As a Collector Edition, this car is number 926 of just 2,391 produced, but more importantly, it is one of only 43 specially designated Daytona 500 Parade Lap cars built for 2002. This example is number 29, corresponding to the starting position of Bill Elliott in that year’s race, giving it a direct tie to one of NASCAR’s most iconic drivers. Its history only gets better from there. This Firebird Trans Am was part of a promotional giveaway following the Daytona 500 and was presented by Jay Leno, who served as the official pace car driver that year. The original contest winner never titled the vehicle and immediately offered it for sale, preserving its early history in a way few cars ever experience. The first titled owner then held onto the car for 19 years before selling it in 2021, with the current owner acquiring it directly and maintaining its integrity ever since. The car comes with an impressive collection of documentation that truly elevates its collectibility. Included are the original window sticker, build sheet, and official letters from Pontiac authenticating its status as a Daytona Parade Lap car. There are also period photos of Jay Leno with the contest winner, along with the original sale listing from when the car first became available. It’s rare to find a car with this level of supporting history—everything that makes the story real is here. This Firebird has lived a well-preserved life, always stored in climate-controlled environments, first in Florida and later in South Carolina. It has been driven and enjoyed as intended, currently showing 67k miles, and will continue to see occasional fair-weather use. Mechanically, it remains very original, with the only modification being drilled and slotted rotors. The brakes have less than 5,000 miles on them, and the tires have under 2,000 miles. Cosmetically, the car presents extremely well for a driven example. It retains original paint throughout with the exception of the front license plate cover, and while there are minor rock chips consistent with use, it remains exceptionally clean overall. The interior is equally well-kept, though like many Firebirds of this era, the door panels do show the common cracking. A clean Carfax report is available and supports the car’s careful ownership history. With its ultra-limited production, documented Daytona 500 connection, celebrity involvement, and extensive original paperwork—including the window sticker—this is a truly standout example of a Collector Edition Firebird Trans Am. Opportunities to own one this complete and this well-documented are few and far between. Price does not include applicable tax, title, license, processing, and/or $240 documentation fees. To see over 80 photos of this car, including the undercarriage, please visit our website www.grautogallery.com
